# Synthetic test images

A fictional weekend travel card pairs a vivid coastline with English and Korean
text, a sample traveler, an example.com email address, and a demo booking number.
Use the photograph for crops and resizing, the headline for highlighting, and the
traveler details for region mosaic or text detection. All details are fictional;
there are no personal screenshots, real reservations, or customer data.

Generated by `scripts/make-fixtures.swift` using macOS drawing and Image I/O.
The committed, AI-generated photo source and its original prompt are documented
in `scripts/fixture-assets/README.md`. The layout and assets are distributed under
the repository's MIT license.

From the repository root, on macOS with access to the system image encoders:

```sh
swift scripts/make-fixtures.swift crates/candy-macos/tests/fixtures
```

- `sample.*`: the same 1000 × 660 card in PNG, JPEG, HEIC and AVIF.
- `orientation6.jpg`: the same card with EXIF orientation 6, for rotation tests.
- `weekend-demo.png`: a 2000 × 1320 rendering for Retina app screenshots. Text is
  drawn at this resolution, not enlarged from the smaller fixture.

Tests create a temporary WebP from the PNG to cover WebP encoding and decoding.
Text-region tests inspect dark glyph pixels on the paper panel, including both
Korean lines, at native resolution and at 4000 × 2640. The photograph is excluded
from glyph-coverage assertions: its texture is not a known text region. As with
any image, review detected boxes before applying a text mosaic.
